identity: University of Amsterdam, English BA programme Linguistics, broad Linguistics track, RIO 56803, registry row 426. The separate Sign Language Linguistics track is outside this comparison.

57077.name: Syntax
57077.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). Introduction to Linguistics or equivalent.
57077.recommendedPriorKnowledge: In order to participate in this course, you need to have passed the course Introduction to Linguistics or have acquired a similar background elsewhere.

57592.name: Czech Language Acquisition 1
57592.recommendedPriorKnowledge: No preliminary knowledge of Czech language is required.

57737.name: Semantics and Pragmatics
57737.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA) or dispensation from the BSA.
57737.recommendedPriorKnowledge: The students have to have basic knowledge of general linguistics, specifically in morphology and syntax. The following courses should be completed before starting Semantics and Pragmatics: Introduction to Linguistics, Morphology, Syntax.

57771.name: Czech Language Acquisition 2
57771.entryRequirements: Completed course Czech Language Acquisition 1 required.

57905.name: Specialization Linguistics
57905.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA) or dispensation from the BSA.
57905.recommendedPriorKnowledge: You build on knowledge from all courses you took in the BA Linguistics or the BA Sign Linguistics (or: all courses in linguistics in the BA NTC). If you are a student in the Bachelor Nederlandse Taal en Cultuur, please contact the course coordinator(s) for consultation. You may need to do some extra preparatory work, especially for the Clinical linguistics Specialization (reading up on neurolinguistic methods).

57954.name: Neurolinguistics
57954.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). You will be automatically allowed access to the course if you have demonstrable knowledge of linguistics (e.g. you completed the course Inleiding Taalwetenschap). Otherwise, you can contact the coordinators on how to obtain sufficient background in linguistics (see below for details).
57954.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Prior knowledge of psycholinguistics and language disorders is recommended, but not mandatory.

57959.name: Transcription
57959.entryRequirements: The Phonetics course from the BA Linguistics.

58039.name: Bachelor's Thesis Linguistics
58039.entryRequirements: Introduction to Linguistics ; a positive bindings study advice (BSA); Linguistic Theories ; having completed the course Specialization Linguistics .
58039.recommendedPriorKnowledge: In principle, the BA thesis is the final subject within the BA programme. Your thesis builds on knowledge acquired during all previous courses you took in the BA Linguistics or the BA Sign Linguistics, including the Specialization course. You should therefore have finished all the obligatory courses of your track before you start writing your thesis.

58226.name: Second Language Acquisition
58226.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). You will be automatically allowed access to the course if you have demonstrable knowledge of linguistics (e.g., you have completed the course Introduction to Linguistics). If you do not have this knowledge, please contact the coordinator of the course.
58226.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Students need some prior knowledge of linguistics. The course Introduction to Linguistics within any of the specific language curricula will suffice. Students who do not have this background should contact the coordinator of the course, and will be asked to read a book about linguistics before entering the course, focusing especially on understanding linguistic sub-domains (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics) and linguistic categories (phonemes, morphemes, constituents, parts of speech). Some knowledge of syntax and phonology is recommended.

58245.name: Philosophy of the Humanities (Language and Cognition)

58286.name: Academic Literacy Test
58286.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Since this is a diagnostic test, there is no need to prepare or study for it.

58309.name: Czech Language Acquisition 4
58309.entryRequirements: Completed course Czech Language Acquisition 3 required.

58364.name: Linguistic Theories
58364.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA); Introduction to Linguistics ; At least one of the following: Phonology OR Syntax OR Semantics and Pragmatics .

58400.name: Czech Language Acquisition 3
58400.entryRequirements: Completed course Czech Language Acquisition 2 required.

59005.name: Phonology
59005.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). Students need to have completed successfully the BA course Introduction to Linguistics.
59005.recommendedPriorKnowledge: You need prior knowledge of linguistics and phonetics. For knowledge of linguistics, the course Introduction to Linguistics (or something similar) will suffice. For knowledge of phonetics, the first-year course in Phonetics would be ideal, while students who take Phonology as a part of their minor Linguistics should make sure that they understand chapters 14 through 16 of the Introduction to Linguistics book: Baker, Anne E. & Hengeveld, Kees (2012), Linguistics . Oxford: Wiley-Blackwell. Or alternatively read Peter Ladefoged's book Vowels and consonants .

59010.name: Psycholinguistics
59010.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). You will be automatically allowed access to the course if you have completed the course Introduction to Linguistics. Otherwise, you can contact the coordinator on how to obtain sufficient background in linguistics.
59010.recommendedPriorKnowledge: You need some prior knowledge of linguistics. The course Introduction to Linguistics within any of the specific language curricula will suffice. Students who do not have this background should contact the course coordinator. These students will be asked to read a book about linguistics before entering the course, focusing especially on understanding the various linguistic disciplines (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics) and on understanding what linguistic categories (phonemes, features, constituents, parts of speech) are. They will also have to form an opinion on what kinds of things all languages share, and what kinds of things tend to differ between languages.

59014.name: First Language Acquisition
59014.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA). You will be automatically allowed access to the course if you have demonstrable knowledge of linguistics (e.g., you completed the course Introduction to Linguistics). Otherwise, you can contact the coordinator on how to obtain sufficient background in linguistics.
59014.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Participants should have at least some prior knowledge of linguistics. The course Introduction to Linguistics within any of the specific language curricula suffices, as does Stemmen van de Stad in the bachelor Nederlandse taal en cultuur . Students who do not have this background should contact the coordinator of the course well in advance of the start of the semester . These students will be asked to read an introductory textbook about linguistics before starting the course, that offers an understanding of (i) the various linguistic disciplines (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics), (ii) what linguistic categories (phonemes, features, constituents, parts of speech) are, and (iii) what kinds of things all languages share, and what kinds of things tend to differ between languages.

59630.name: Sociolinguistics
59630.entryRequirements: You should have taken the preceding courses of the first year.

60788.name: Speech Processing
60788.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA) or dispensation from the BSA.
60788.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Knowledge of the contents of the first-year course Phonetics is assumed. Students who have not taken that course can read Vowels and Consonants by Ladefoged and Disner (2012).

60791.name: Research Methods & Statistics
60791.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA) or dispensation from the BSA.

60974.name: First-Year Research Project
60974.entryRequirements: There are no formal entry requirements.
60974.recommendedPriorKnowledge: You are expected to be familiar with research in the domains of language and/or cognition.

61031.name: Introduction to Clinical Linguistics
61031.entryRequirements: A positive binding study advice (BSA) or dispensation from the BSA.
61031.recommendedPriorKnowledge: You will be automatically allowed access to the course if you have demonstrable knowledge of linguistics (e.g., you completed the course Introduction to Linguistics). Otherwise, you can contact the course coordinator on how to obtain sufficient background in linguistics. Background on basic psycholinguistic concepts and theories are also preferable.

sourceUse: The Part B adopted 9 June 2026 confirms the 60 EC first year, 72 EC upper-year core, 6 EC Philosophy of the Humanities, 30 EC free electives and 12 EC thesis. Appendix 1 and the dated course guide agree on the broad track. The Catalan branch has no listed offerings in the dated grid. Czech is the first complete documented sequence in guide order and is eligible for the broad track; its four modules are taught in English. The 6 EC Specialization Linguistics is one required unit. No compulsory placement is listed.

progression.firstYear: Phonetics is in block 2 and is required for Transcription in block 3. Introduction to Linguistics and the earlier formal study precede Sociolinguistics. The first-year project follows in block 6 and has no additional formal entry requirements. Czech 1–4 run in blocks 1, 2, 4 and 5 with each completed course required for the next.
progression.secondYear: Positive binding study advice is the general progression gate. Introduction to Linguistics supplies entry background for the main acquisition, processing and structural courses. Linguistic Theories in block 6 requires positive BSA, Introduction to Linguistics and at least one of Phonology, Syntax and Semantics and Pragmatics, all placed earlier in year two.
progression.thirdYear: Speech Processing and Research Methods & Statistics precede the required 6 EC Specialization Linguistics in spring block 4. The regular thesis follows in blocks 5–6 after Specialization Linguistics. It also requires positive BSA and completion of Introduction to Linguistics and Linguistic Theories. The 30 EC open space may span both semesters. External courses need permission and introductory electives have the specified 12 EC default cap and limited exceptions.
